title: Consolidated Digital Marketing Performance Report — Google Ads & Klaviyo data validation, analysis, recommendations, and a branded stakeholder presentation
goal: Analyze and consolidate both Google Ads, Google Product data exports and Klaviyo (Email and SMS) performance data to identify key insights and optimization opportunities, and create a clear, stakeholder-ready digital marketing performance report.
context:
Consolidated Marketing Report: As part of my digital marketing role, I regularly analyze campaign performance across multiple digital marketing platforms and translate the results into reports that stakeholders can easily understand and act on. Reporting can become time-consuming when data comes from different platforms and needs to be consolidated, checked for accuracy, analyzed, and converted into meaningful insights.
For this task, I will use exported and privacy-safe Google Ads and Klaviyo (Email and SMS) campaign data rather than accessing live client accounts during the recorded session due to an NDA. My workflow will use Claude to help consolidate and analyze the data, identify important performance trends, develop optimization recommendations, and ultimately support the creation of a clear and visually engaging performance report.

session_goal_achievement.Why or why not: It produced an accurate, consolidated, visually appealing Marketing Report including key highlights from each channel as well as recommendations and next steps in a visually appealing branded report.

Step-1.step_name: Prepare, consolidate and validate campaign data
Step-1.step_action: Upload privacy-safe Excel exports containing Google Ads, Google Product data and Klaviyo Email and SMS performance data. Review the structure of each dataset, identify and standardize comparable fields and metrics, flag missing or inconsistent data, and consolidate the relevant information into a structured dataset for further analysis.

nodes.label: Prepare the data to scope the consolidation task
nodes.detail: Sets up a working folder, adds her own custom 'campaign-report-analyst' Claude Skill, and assigns Claude the role of data-preparation/validation analyst for the whole workflow. Explains the four raw privacy-safe exports and their differing date windows (Google Ads week-over-week vs. Klaviyo full-month) before uploading and submitting them.

nodes.label: Prepare 'campaign-report-analyst' Claude Skill so Claude can perform the task as a data-preparation/validation analyst
nodes.detail: Sets up a working folder, adds her own custom 'campaign-report-analyst' Claude Skill, and assigns Claude the role of data-preparation/validation analyst for the whole workflow. Explains the four raw privacy-safe exports and their differing date windows (Google Ads week-over-week vs. Klaviyo full-month) before uploading and submitting them.

nodes.label: Explains the four raw privacy-safe exports and their differing date windows (Google Ads week-over-week vs. Klaviyo full-month) before uploading and submitting them to Claude.
nodes.detail: Sets up a working folder, adds her own custom 'campaign-report-analyst' Claude Skill, and assigns Claude the role of data-preparation/validation analyst for the whole workflow. Explains the four raw privacy-safe exports and their differing date windows (Google Ads week-over-week vs. Klaviyo full-month) before uploading and submitting them.

nodes.label: Consolidate and validate the four raw exports into one workbook
nodes.detail: Explores every sheet, checks date ranges, reconciles Klaviyo subtotals, and de-duplicates the Google Ads product file, then builds a 7-tab consolidated workbook (Overview, GAds Account Summary, GAds Campaign Type, GAds Product Level, Klaviyo Email, Klaviyo SMS, Data Quality Log) flagging the date-window mismatch and a year typo as the two issues needing resolution.

nodes.label: Review and save the consolidated workbook and validation findings
nodes.detail: Reads through each tab (Overview, Google Ads performance, product list, campaign/flow detail) and the Data Quality Log's 16 findings, confirming the flagged issues (149 repeated product titles, 6 duplicate zero-activity rows, missing-price/volatile-swing products) look correct before saving the file.

Step-2.step_action: Analyze the validated Google Ads and Klaviyo Email/SMS data prepared in Step 1. Compare current and prior-period Google Ads performance, examine Search and Performance Max results, review product-level performance, and assess Klaviyo Email and SMS campaign and flow performance. Identify the most commercially important positive and negative trends, material changes, unusual values and performance anomalies. Clearly distinguish between confirmed numerical findings, descriptive observations and unresolved measurement limitations.

nodes.label: Design and send prompt to Claude for requesting performance analysis
nodes.detail: Reuses the already-written Step 2 action text, attaches the validated Step 1 workbook, and specifies the required cross-channel output structure before submitting the prompt.

nodes.label: Deliver the Step 2 cross-channel performance analysis
nodes.detail: Computes Search-vs-PMax share, product-level concentration and email/SMS campaign-vs-flow performance, then produces a markdown analysis tagging every claim as Confirmed, Observation or Question. Headlines: Performance Max softened on every metric despite being 90% of spend, one email flow drove 28.5% of July email revenue, and flows outperform campaigns but carry higher unsubscribe rates.

nodes.label: Review and download the headline findings and open the full analysis
nodes.detail: Listens to the three headline findings, notes that Section 8 lists items needing verification before Step 3, and downloads the markdown file to read in full.

nodes.label: Formulate corrections to two of Claude's flagged limitations
nodes.detail: Reads Section 8 closely and disagrees with two points: the Google Ads/Klaviyo date-window mismatch is intentional agency practice (weekly hourly-moving Google data vs. monthly slower-lifecycle email/SMS), and the 542-product list may be a top-N cutoff rather than the full catalog. Sends both corrections to Claude.

nodes.label: Reclassify the date-window design and flag the product-list uncertainty
nodes.detail: Updates the document to note the date-window difference as intentional design rather than a limitation, but explains it cannot confirm from the data alone whether the 542-product list is capped, and asks two clarifying questions before it can resolve the caveat.

nodes.label: Review the revision and answer the product-list questions
nodes.detail: Confirms the 542-product list is simply the full active catalog size and is not capped, resolving Claude's open question.

nodes.label: Finalize the analysis by clearing the resolved caveat
nodes.detail: Removes the top-N caveat throughout the document now that the product list is confirmed to be the complete active catalog, leaving only genuine open items (unattributed Google Ads spend, a thin-data product) in Section 8.

nodes.label: Download the finalized cross-channel performance analysis
nodes.detail: Downloads the corrected Step 2 analysis file to the working folder before proceeding.

Step-3.step_name: Investigate the drivers behind performance changes
Step-3.step_action: Use the key performance trends and anomalies identified in Step 2 to investigate what may be driving the changes in performance. Cross-reference the validated Google Ads account, campaign-type and product-level data with Klaviyo Email and SMS activity. Assess whether changes in advertising spend, traffic, conversion volume, campaign-type mix, product performance or lifecycle-marketing activity appear to be associated with the results.

nodes.label: Compose and submit diagnostic-driver request
nodes.detail: States the diagnostic requirements (confirmed relationship vs. evidence-supported hypothesis vs. alternative explanation vs. unresolved question for each driver), briefly interrupts herself to properly attach the corrected Step 2 file, then resubmits.

nodes.label: Generate an output for diagnosing performance drivers by cross-referencing Google Ads and Klaviyo but the generation process got interrupted
nodes.detail: Runs a counterfactual check showing Search is quietly propping up the account's efficiency gain, then cross-references Klaviyo campaign/flow names against Google Ads products, finding a genuine split (Halloween products grew with a matching SMS push; Mirror Mi and LOL Surprise show email revenue with no matching Google Ads spend; Batman got the heaviest lifecycle push yet its Google Ads product declined). Explicitly flags that Klaviyo has no send-date field, so 'coincides with' only means same product line and month.

nodes.label: Upload supporting files generated from the previous step to Claude and resend a revised prompt
Generate diagnostic driver analysis
Review diagnostic findings, save files, and confirm evidence caveats
nodes.detail: Reads the three headline diagnoses and the ranked list of areas for Step 4, then downloads the diagnostic document before moving on.

Step-4.step_action: Use the performance trends and diagnostic findings from Steps 2 and 3 to develop practical optimization recommendations across Google Ads and Klaviyo Email/SMS. Evaluate the potential business impact of each recommendation, provide a rationale supported by the analysis, and prioritize actions according to importance and expected impact.

nodes.label: Requests a practical optimization recommendations by combining the answers from step 2 and step 3
nodes.detail: Requests a prioritized optimization plan with recommended actions, rationale, expected impact and affected channels, noting all prior outputs are already saved in-chat so no re-upload is needed.

nodes.label: Generate a prioritized optimization plan across Google Ads and Klaviyo
nodes.detail: Produces 13 ranked recommendations scored on Impact, Confidence and Effort, carrying Step 3's confidence levels through honestly (e.g. capping the Search budget test at 'phased' rather than a full reallocation given low-base uncertainty).

nodes.label: Review the generated diagnosis driver from Step 3
nodes.detail: Reads the top priorities (audit Performance Max rather than cut it, a phased Search budget test, two cheap content fixes, templating the BackInStock flow) and the 'deliberately not recommended' section, then downloads the plan before moving to Step 5.

nodes.label: Review quickly and save the prioritized recommendations and rationale
nodes.detail: Reads the top priorities (audit Performance Max rather than cut it, a phased Search budget test, two cheap content fixes, templating the BackInStock flow) and the 'deliberately not recommended' section, then downloads the plan before moving to Step 5.

Step-5.step_name: Develop the reporting narrative and presentation structure
Step-5.step_action: Synthesize the validated data, key performance findings, identified performance drivers and prioritized recommendations from Steps 1-4 into a clear reporting narrative. Organize the information into a logical slide-by-slide structure that highlights the most commercially important insights, explains what happened and why, and connects each finding to a recommended action. Export this to Google slides.

nodes.label: Request Claude to synthesize findings into a slide narrative
nodes.detail: Writes a detailed prompt asking Claude to synthesize Steps 1-4 into a slide-by-slide narrative connecting findings to recommendations, mentioning Google Slides as the intended export target.

nodes.label: Build a Powerpoint and quality-check a 15-slide cross-channel performance deck
nodes.detail: Finds no dedicated Google Slides connector and builds a PowerPoint instead, constructing all 15 slides (exec summary, methodology, channel findings, drivers, recommendations, next steps) with iterative visual QA that catches and fixes two real bugs (a wrong-direction trend arrow, overlapping timeline cards), pausing once on a tool-use limit before finishing and validating the full deck.

nodes.label: Save the generated slides and review it against client expectations, judging it 'basically the ideal report,' with the only complaint being its generic unbranded styling and some decorative circles she dislikes
nodes.detail: Opens and reads through the report — headline numbers, Google Ads account performance, prioritized recommendations — judging it 'basically the ideal report,' with the only complaint being its generic unbranded styling and some decorative circles she dislikes.

Step-6.step_name: Branding, design optimization, quality-check and finalize the stakeholder-ready performance report.
Step-6.step_action: Use the approved narrative and presentation structure from Step 5 to create the final visual report referencing the existing branded presentation template attached as the visual guideline insights and recommendations before finalizing the Google Slides output.

nodes.label: Navigate back to the chat to scope the final branding step
nodes.detail: Acknowledges branding is optional but decides to complete it anyway, navigating back to the chat to pick up where Step 5 left off.

nodes.label: Send a prompt about the branding request with the agency template attached
nodes.detail: Instructs Claude to apply the look and feel of her attached 'Candy Consult' branded presentation template instead of the generic Step 5 styling, mentions Gamma as a possible design-improvement tool, and explicitly reiterates that the output must be genuinely on-brand, not just a token pass.

nodes.label: Extract the brand template's design system and rebuild the deck end-to-end, offering to use Gamma
nodes.detail: Inspects the template's underlying XML to pull exact colors, fonts and layout patterns, rebuilds all 13 slides to match, runs iterative visual QA that catches and fixes two layout bugs, then runs an explicit accuracy/consistency review against the Step 1-4 source data that catches and corrects two real errors (a miscalculated SMS performance multiple and an overstated efficiency claim) before finalizing.

nodes.label: Confirm the final branded report meets stakeholder expectations
nodes.detail: Reviews the header/what-happened/what-to-do-next structure, the Google Ads and Klaviyo scope callouts, and the prioritized next-steps section in the new Candy Consult brand, concluding this is exactly the kind of report a client would want — completing the session's goal.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: The agent understood the task, context, and instructions provided. No clarifying questions needed.

Step 3.step_name: Investigate the drivers behind performance changes
Step 3.step_action: Use the key performance trends and anomalies identified in Step 2 to investigate what may be driving the changes in performance. Cross-reference the validated Google Ads account, campaign-type and product-level data with Klaviyo Email and SMS activity. Assess whether changes in advertising spend, traffic, conversion volume, campaign-type mix, product performance or lifecycle-marketing activity appear to be associated with the results.
Step 3.input: The final validated consolidated dataset from Step 1 and the key performance trends, material changes and anomalies identified in Step 2. This includes: Google Ads account-level current-versus-prior-week findings, Search versus Performance Max findings, product-level performance trends and data-quality flags, Klaviyo Email campaign-versus-flow findings, Klaviyo SMS campaign-versus-flow findings, the prioritised trend register from Step 2, unresolved attribution, metric-definition and reconciliation limitations.
Step 3.output: A structured diagnostic analysis identifying: 1. The most important potential drivers of the Google Ads account-level changes, 2. The contribution of Search and Performance Max to those changes, 3. Product-level factors associated with growth or underperformance, 4. Klaviyo Email and SMS activity that coincides with relevant performance patterns, 5. Evidence supporting or weakening each proposed driver, 6. Confidence levels for each diagnostic conclusion, 7. Questions or evidence gaps requiring human verification, 8. A prioritised list of areas that should proceed to recommendation development in Step 4.
Step 3.tools: 1.Paid version: Claude Max, 2.Paid version: Microsoft Excel
rubrics: Every proposed performance driver is supported by specific evidence from the validated Step 1 workbook or the confirmed Step 2 findings
The diagnostic analysis correctly distinguishes between correlation, plausible contribution and proven causation
Google Ads account, campaign-type, product-level and Klaviyo lifecycle activity are cross-referenced without incorrectly combining incompatible reporting periods or attribution metrics
Alternative explanations, data limitations and unresolved questions are clearly documented rather than hidden or converted into assumptions
The analysis prioritises the most commercially significant drivers and creates a clear evidence-based handoff for Step 4 without prematurely recommending actions.

ratings.output_quality_reason: Rubric 1: 5/5, Reason: It directly investigates Search's ROAS improvement, PMax softening, product-level declines, lifecycle performance and the main anomalies identified previously, Rubric 2: 4/5, Reason: The majority of claims are quantified and sourced from the validated data. However, some hypotheses rely partly on general marketing assumptions, such as PMax typically producing lower CTR, rather than evidence available in this dataset, Rubric 3: 5/5, Reason: The GEAH, Halloween, Mirror Mi, LOL Surprise, Batman and Cartuned comparisons are useful, and Claude appropriately acknowledges the lack of matching send dates and the inferential nature of product-name matching, Rubric 4: 5/5, Reason: This is probably the strongest aspect of the output. Claude explicitly separates confirmed numerical relationships, evidence-supported hypotheses, alternative explanations and unresolved questions throughout, Rubric 5: 5/5, Reason: The final prioritised list gives Step 4 a very clear starting point, led by Search, PMax, the product/PMax reconciliation gap and the largest cross-channel opportunities.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: Claude successfully investigated the key performance changes rather than simply restating Step 2. It decomposed the Google Ads account-level movements, explored product-level and lifecycle-marketing relationships, challenged its own hypotheses with alternative explanations, assigned confidence levels, and identified evidence gaps that require human verification. The output substantially reduced the manual work required to diagnose the dataset, although some calculations and interpretations still required human quality control.

Step 4.input: Consolidated and validated dataset from Step 1, Performance trends and anomalies identified in Step 2, Performance drivers and diagnostic findings from Step 3
Step 4.output: A prioritized optimization plan outlining recommended actions, supporting rationale, expected impact and the channels or areas affected.
Step 4.tools: Paid version: Claude Max, Paid version: Microsoft Excel

Each recommendation is supported by evidence from the available data
Recommendations are specific and actionable rather than generic marketing advice

The recommendations cover the relevant Google Ads and Klaviyo opportunities without making unsupported assumptions.

Step 5.step_name: Develop the reporting narrative and presentation structure
Step 5.step_action: Synthesize the validated data, key performance findings, identified performance drivers and prioritized recommendations from Steps 1-4 into a clear reporting narrative. Organize the information into a logical slide-by-slide structure that highlights the most commercially important insights, explains what happened and why, and connects each finding to a recommended action. Export this to Google slides.
Step 5.input: The validated consolidated dataset from Step 1, Key trends and channel findings from Step 2, Diagnostic findings from Step 3, Prioritized optimization recommendations from Step 4.
Step 5.output: A structured presentation draft outline in Google slides and report content, including an executive summary, key performance findings, channel insights, performance drivers, optimization recommendations and proposed next steps.
Step 5.tools: 1.Paid version: Claude Max, 2. Free: Google Slides
rubrics: The reporting narrative accurately reflects the findings from Steps 1–4
The presentation follows a clear flow from performance → insight → cause → action
The most commercially important findings are prioritized
Recommendations are clearly connected to supporting data
The draft content is concise and suitable for a non-technical stakeholder.

ratings.output_quality_reason: Rubric 1: 4/5, Reason: The deck faithfully carries forward the major Google Ads, product, Email, SMS, diagnostic and recommendation findings. However, it also carries forward a few overstated conclusions and one inaccurate comparison, Rubric 2: 5/5, Reason: The sequencing is very strong: executive summary → methodology → performance → channel detail → drivers → recommendations → next steps, Rubric 3: 5/5, Reason: Search efficiency, PMax softening, BackInStock performance, product anomalies and cross-channel opportunities are appropriately prioritised, Rubric 4: 5/5, Reason: The recommendation slides explicitly link actions such as the PMax audit and Search budget test back to quantified findings, Rubric 5: 5/5, Reason: The content is substantially more concise than the underlying analysis and uses clear summaries, callouts and action-oriented language.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: Claude successfully converted a large amount of technical campaign analysis into a structured, stakeholder-ready presentation narrative. It reduced the complexity of the underlying data, prioritised the main commercial findings, connected insights to recommendations and created a logical slide-by-slide story that would have required significant manual effort to develop.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: Claude successfully converted the approved analysis and reporting narrative into a concise, branded and stakeholder-ready presentation.
